findings.consequence: A user cannot read NASA's latest revision through crc-sdk, and the default (1.0) is the oldest. The differences seen here are small; other models, variables and regions were not compared. NASA's technical note for version 2.0 (31 May 2025, section 4.3) states that tasmax and tasmin were reprocessed in their entirety with a corrected observational reference (an artifact over central Canada) and that values were swapped in grid cells where the maximum was below the minimum; that anomalously large pr values in cells with an extremely small daily climatology were adjusted; and that bounds were applied to hurs, huss, rlds and sfcWind. These corrections are in version 2.0 only.
findings.documented: docs/sources/cmip6.md:73: 'File revisions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are selected explicitly'. crc_sdk/workflows/nex.py:84-85 refuses any other version.
evidence: NASA technical note for version 2.0, sections 3.2.2.1 and 4.3 (docs/validation/references/nex-gddp-cmip6-v2/README.md)
findings.note: From 1.0 the highest version on NASA listing is read, so version 2.0 is read by default (checks file[*], run of 2026-11-24 on crc-sdk 1.0.0). What cannot be requested is now the older revisions: CRC-031-NEX.
findings.observed: For ACCESS-CM2 r1i1p1f1, NASA's archive holds files ending in _v2.0.nc for tasmax, tasmin and pr, in both years checked (historical 2014, ssp585 2050). They were uploaded on 1 July 2025 and carry the attribute version = '2.0'. No version 1.2 file exists for these; version 1.1 exists for pr only. In the Texas box the annual one-day rainfall from 2.0 equals that from 1.1 and differs from 1.0 in 15 of 2,158 cells in 2014 (by at most 0.08 mm) and 42 cells in 2050 (by at most 0.84 mm); the annual maximum temperature from 2.0 equals that from 1.0.
findings.title: NASA serves files of version 2.0, which cannot be requested

findings.consequence: A small share of pixels (about 3 in 10,000 here) that have depths at four or more return periods get no curve although one exists, and nothing in the output says so. Whether a pixel is fitted depends on the last digits of its depths.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:33-39 says the plan 'caches AOI crops, then fits'; no page says that a fit can fail. crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:432-433 raises 'quantile optimizer did not converge' when crc-framework's fit_quantiles reports no convergence, and the curated JRC policy sets on_fit_failure = 'skip' (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:53).
evidence: check records jrc-flood/curves[glofas-tx], curves[glofas-houston], curves[glofas-fremont], curves[efas-rhine] (site/validation/data/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.note: From 1.0 crc-sdk fits no JRC curve by default, and an explicit fit that fails raises, warns or keeps a failure row, so the silent drop is gone. The dependence of convergence on how the depths are represented continues as CRC-026-FWK.
findings.observed: A least-squares line through the same points has an exact solution; the independent reference computes it for every such pixel. crc-framework 0.6.0 does not return one for 2,821 pixels of the Texas box, 82 of the Houston box, 5 of the Fremont box and 49 of the Rhine box (0 of the Austin box); the Houston and Austin boxes lie inside the Texas box. Each has several equal depths followed by larger ones, for example 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2.639, 3.768 m. Called directly, fit_quantiles(family='gumbel_r') on that series raises 'gumbel_r fitting did not converge after 374 iterations' when the depths are the 32-bit numbers of the file, and converges after 91 iterations when the same depths are given as decimal numbers. crc-sdk writes no row and no message for these pixels. For every pixel both sides fitted, location and scale agree within 1.2e-6 m (two of 19,702,276 parameters in the Texas box differ by more than the tolerance of 1e-6 m, the larger by 1.1e-6 m).
findings.title: The quantile fit gives up on depths that are flat and then rise, and crc-sdk then drops the pixel without a message

findings.consequence: A place the publisher's map floods only at long return periods (100 years and more), or at a constant 1 m, is absent from the output in the same way as a place that never floods. A user reading the output as 'no row means no flood' undercounts flooded area by the shares above. The pixels left out for equal or decreasing depths are permanent water bodies, where the publisher patched its maps (1 m is the patch value seen); those left out for fewer than four depths are land the publisher's map floods only at the longer return periods, about half of all pixels left out in the Texas box.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md does not mention pixels left out. The rules are in the code: four or more finite depths (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:658-663), a fit failure is skipped (adapters.py:702-716, crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:53), and the curated policy writes no diagnostics file (jrc.py:57-81).
evidence: check records jrc-flood/curves[*] and exploration tables 'Wet pixels that get no curve', 'Published wet pixels without a curve, by return period' (site/validation/data/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.note: From 1.0 a pixel with two or three depths or with equal depths is delivered (checks delivered[*], run of 2026-11-24 on crc-sdk 1.0.0, crc-sdk reading the copy of the publisher's files held (the publisher's server did not answer)). Pixels with one depth or a decreasing depth are still left out: CRC-023-JRC.
findings.observed: Share of the pixels that have a depth at some return period and get no curve: Texas box 1,832,251 of 11,686,210 (15.7%), Houston 65,705 of 278,654 (23.6%), Austin 3,293 of 25,494 (12.9%), Fremont 2,734 of 10,603 (25.8%), Rhine (EFAS) 18,824 of 161,898 (11.6%). By cause in the Texas box: fewer than four depths 941,251; all depths equal 698,317 (every one of them at exactly 1 m at every return period); a depth lower than at a shorter return period 192,683; the fit not converging 2,821 (CRC-013-FWK). At the 500-year return period 1,832,250 of the 11,686,209 flooded pixels of the Texas box have no curve; at 10 years 890,968 of 9,255,575. The reference applies the same rules and names the same pixels, apart from those of CRC-013-FWK. findings.consequence: Evaluated at 10 to 50 years, the output shows water where the publisher's map has none and negative depths where it has water; the documentation says the values are not bit-for-bit but gives no size. findings.consequence: Outputs for two boxes cannot be joined, compared or de-duplicated on source_id, and the same request with and without a cache gives different ids for the same pixel.

The Fremont box read as two overlapping boxes gives the same identifier, cell and knots for all 2,109 shared pixels (check overlap[glofas-fremont], run of 2026-11-24 on crc-sdk 1.0.0, crc-sdk reading the copy of the publisher's files held (the publisher's server did not answer)).
findings.observed: source_id is the SHA-256 of the dataset name, the tile and the pixel's row and column (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:299-301, 741-743); with a cache the row and column are those of the local crop (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:502-511). All 22,201 fitted pixels of the Austin box are also in the Texas-box output with the same curve (difference of location 0); of 2,000 of them compared, 0 have the same source_id in the two outputs. Per area, the ids equal the reference's computed from the crop position in every sampled pixel, and equal the position in the publisher's file in 0 of 2,000 (621 of 2,000 in the Texas box, where the crops of two tiles begin at the tile's first row and column). Without a cache the position is the file's (read in the code, not run).

The message says the resources are missing or invalid, though the files are present and unchanged.

A run in offline mode from another working folder, given the absolute path of the same cache, ends with FileNotFoundError 'cems-glofas-river-flood cannot be materialized offline; missing or invalid cached AOI resources: ID18_N40_W130:RP10, ...'; from the working folder the cache was made in, the same run completes. findings.consequence: A user asking for a state or a country should expect tens of minutes and several GB per run, with nothing kept if the run stops before the end; a larger box may not fit in memory. One machine, one run.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md gives no time or size. Its example is a box of 0.7 by 0.5 degrees.
findings.observed: GloFAS for the Texas box (201,757,502 pixels in four tiles, 9,851,138 curves, 10,703,386 rows): 1,604 s and a peak of 5,804 MB on an arm64 Mac with 16 GB, the 28 crops (about 0.6 GB at the publisher) fetched in the same run. The smaller boxes took 10 s (Austin, 22,201 curves) to 54 s (Houston, 212,867 curves). Read in the code: the output file is written only at the end of the run.

sources.notes: Assessed at crc-sdk 0.11.2: the statement, the code references and the records below describe that version. The port to 1.0 is pending. Draft. Assessed on the 1.5 degree store (wb2-1p5), the Texas box (80 grid cells), the rainfall recipes for 2021, with and without the land mask. One variable-year of this store is about 0.9 GB whatever the box, because every chunk covers the globe. The temperature recipes, the 0.25 degree store and the fitted curves were not run.
sources.publisher: ECMWF / Copernicus C3S (public Zarr copies by Google and WeatherBench2)
sources.purpose: A historical baseline of annual temperature and rainfall extremes on H3 cells, comparable with the projection recipes.

statement.note: Confirmed for wb2-1p5 only. arco-0p25 was not opened: one variable-year there is about 8,800 global chunks.
statement.text: Opens one of two public Zarr copies of hourly ERA5 anonymously, with zarr over gcsfs: `arco-0p25` (the default, gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3, 0.25 degree) or `wb2-1p5` (gs://weatherbench2/datasets/era5/1959-2022-1h-240x121_equiangular_with_poles_conservative.zarr, 1.5 degree). No checksum of the hourly data is taken.

Names the release `final-through-<date>`. The date is the store's `valid_time_stop` attribute; for a store without it (wb2-1p5) it is 31 December of a year written in the code, 2022. Only `latest` or that name is accepted.

Accepts the years from the store's first year (1959 for wb2-1p5, written in the code) to the last complete year of that release; for rainfall the last year must be followed by one more day of record. The years are not compared with the store's time axis: hours the axis does not hold are skipped without an error.
Decodes the time axis from its `units` attribute (`hours`, `days` or `seconds since <date>`) as whole numbers; the `calendar` attribute is not read. Days are UTC days.
Reads `2m_temperature` for `txx` and `tnn` and `total_precipitation` for `rx1day` and `rx5day`, and requires the array to have exactly the dimensions time, latitude and longitude, in any order.

statement.note: The check confirms that the assumption holds for wb2-1p5 today. That the attribute is not read is shown in the offline tests on a constructed store that declares another unit (see finding CRC-006-ERA5).
statement.text: Assumes 2 m temperature in kelvin and precipitation in metres. The `units` attribute the store declares for the variable is not read.

statement.note: Confirmed for a box of 8 by 10 cells. A box narrower than one cell and a box at the 180 degree meridian were not run.
statement.text: Selects the grid cells whose centres lie inside the box grown by half a cell on every side, with longitudes brought to -180..180 and ordered west to east. A box narrower than one cell is widened to two cells. The same box is applied a second time to the stored annual file.
With `land_only`, keeps a cell only where the store's `land_sea_mask` is 0.5 or more; the others get no value.

statement.note: The chunks read from the publisher hold no NaN in the box. Missing hours inside a chunk were exercised in the offline tests only; absent chunks were exercised by the years the reference copy does not hold. The reading of an absent chunk as NaN is zarr's behaviour and has no line in crc-sdk.
statement.text: Treats a value that is not finite as missing. A chunk the store does not hold is read as the array's fill value (NaN), so it is missing too, without an error.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft (one variable-year is about 0.7 GB). Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: Subtracts 273.15 from every hourly temperature, before any reduction, to give degrees Celsius.
Multiplies every hourly precipitation value by 1,000, before any reduction, to give millimetres.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: The daily maximum (`txx`) or minimum (`tnn`) is taken over the hours stamped 00:00 to 23:00 UTC; a day needs at least 18 of its 24 hours.
An hourly precipitation value is counted in the UTC day of its stamp less one hour (the value stamped 00:00 belongs to the day before). A day is the sum of its 24 hours and needs all 24.

statement.note: In the year read every cell has 364 of 365 days, so the 90 per cent line itself was crossed only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Gives a grid cell an annual value only when at least 90 per cent of the year's days have a value (329 of 365, 330 of 366).

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: `txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.

`rx1day` is the largest daily total of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum over five consecutive days that all have a value and lie within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years.

statement.note: The 32-bit rounding is confirmed by the annual values. The manifest and the reuse of stored years were not exercised: every run used an empty cache folder.
statement.text: Keeps each year's values for the recipe and area as 32-bit floats in one small NetCDF file, listed with its checksum in a manifest; the annual values returned are those 32-bit values. Hourly data is never kept. The file's name does not depend on the release.

`annual_extremes()` returns one row per year and grid cell that has a value: year, latitude and longitude of the cell centre as the store writes them (longitude in -180..180), value in the recipe's unit; ordered by year, then in the store's latitude order, then west to east.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitting belongs to a later tier. A request of four years was accepted and one of fewer was not tried (finding CRC-002-FWK is about this rule).
statement.text: Refuses a request of fewer years than `minimum_years` (20 by default, never fewer than 4). Each grid cell is then fitted when it has at least 4 annual values.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitted curve (family, method, assignment to H3 cells) belongs to a later tier.
statement.text: Fits to each cell's annual values a generalised extreme value distribution by sample L-moments (the default for all four recipes), on H3 cells of resolution 5 by default, and writes the canonical hazard file.

statement.note: Not checked: these labels are written when the curve is fitted, which this draft does not run. `annual_extremes()` returns the four value columns only.
statement.text: Labels the fitted file with the store's address, the licence CC-BY-4.0, a Copernicus attribution with the retrieval year, the retrieval time, a checksum of the annual files' checksums, the window of years, `single_member` pooling and `annual_exceedance`.

sources.adds: Nothing is added to the values, and no unit is converted. crc-sdk downloads NOAA's file of all storms (ALL), keeps a checksummed copy, and for one agency returns two rows per track point: the agency's wind in knots and its pressure in hPa, as numbers, at IBTrACS's combined position, with longitudes moved into -180..180 and an H3 cell. A point the agency did not report keeps its rows, with no value and a failure code. Of NOAA's 174 columns six are read; the season, basin, name, track type and the agency's own position are not returned. Licence text, attribution, checksum and retrieval time travel with the output.
sources.compared: NOAA's ALL file is downloaded independently and read with Python's csv module; for each of the ten agencies every row crc-sdk returns is recomputed from the file and compared field by field, in order (about 1.46 million rows per agency). The address, the bytes, the declared units and the provenance attached to the output are checked separately.
sources.notes: Assessed by default: no selection, each agency read in full. The output covers every point of the file for every agency, so most rows of most agencies carry no value. The position is the combined LAT and LON of IBTrACS, not the agency's own position columns. Times are ISO_TIME with a T and no zone designator; NOAA's times are UTC. Where a track crosses the date line NOAA's longitudes exceed 180 (up to 266.9); crc-sdk moves them into -180..180. It does so by arithmetic on every longitude, so for many points (350,339 of 730,694 in the file of 2026-11-24) the delivered longitude is not the number nearest to NOAA's decimal value but differs from it by at most 3e-14 degrees; the identifier, which hashes the position, then cannot be rebuilt from NOAA's text. In NOAA's file SEASON runs to 2027 because southern-hemisphere seasons are labelled by their second year; crc-sdk does not return it.
sources.purpose: Native storm point observations for one reporting agency: its maximum sustained wind and minimum central pressure at each track point, as published, for inspection. Not asset winds or return-period curves.

statement.text: Requests one file for every agency: `<root>/ibtracs.ALL.list.v04r01.csv`, NOAA's file of all storms. No basin or period file can be chosen.
Saves the response unchanged and identifies it by the SHA-256 of its bytes. No announced length or publisher checksum is compared.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing that a reused copy is stale needs NOAA to change the file between two runs. Left to monitoring.
statement.text: `Runtime()` keeps no cache, so every read downloads the file again. With `Cache.reuse(path)` a file already indexed for the address is served by its recorded checksum without asking NOAA whether it has changed; `Cache.offline(path)` never downloads and fails if the file is not cached; `Cache.refresh(path)` downloads again.

Reads six of NOAA's columns: SID, ISO_TIME, LAT, LON and the agency's `<AGENCY>_WIND` and `<AGENCY>_PRES`; the read fails if one is absent. The other columns (season, basin, name, nature, track type, distance to land, the agency's own position and radii) are not returned.

Reads line 2 of the file as units: the agency's wind must be `kts` or `knots` and its pressure `mb` or `hPa`, or the read fails. Declares the wind in knots and the pressure in hPa; no value is converted. The wind of agency USA is declared as a 60-second average; no averaging period is declared for the other agencies.

Returns observations with twelve columns: variable_id, scenario_id, period_id, support_id, cell_id, geometry, time, value, station_id, group_id, failure, coverage. The schema metadata of every batch carries the evidence metadata as JSON under `crc.evidence`.
Removes leading and trailing whitespace from every value before it is used.
The time is ISO_TIME with its space replaced by `T` (for example `2023-06-08T12:00:00`); it must parse as a date and time, or the read fails. No time zone is added.

Parses LAT and LON as numbers; a longitude outside -180..360 or a latitude outside -90..90 fails the read. The longitude is moved into -180..180 as `(lon + 180) % 360 - 180`, so 180 becomes -180. The point is written as little-endian WKB. It is IBTrACS's combined position, not the agency's own.
Adds the H3 cell of resolution 9 that contains the point.

variable_id is `ibtracs:<AGENCY>:maximum_sustained_wind` or `ibtracs:<AGENCY>:minimum_central_pressure`. support_id is `<SID>:<time>@` followed by the first 20 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the WKB point. group_id is the SID. station_id, scenario_id and period_id are null.
Parses the agency's wind and pressure as floating-point numbers; a value that is not a finite number fails the read.
A value that is empty after trimming becomes a null value with the failure code `source_no_data` and the message 'The source reports no valid observation.'. coverage is null.

Returns two rows for every data row of the file, the wind and then the pressure, in the file's order, whether or not the agency reported a value there. No row is dropped, merged or sorted; two rows with the same identity fail the read.

Attaches a source identity to the metadata, to the report and to every batch's schema metadata: provider `ibtracs`, product `ibtracs_v04r01_tracks`, member the agency, and one resource with the address, the SHA-256, the licence text 'NOAA open-use terms; originator terms may apply', the attribution 'NOAA NCEI IBTrACS v04r01, doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16' and the retrieval time in UTC. The release is `ibtracs:selected-source-snapshot` with a SHA-256 over the sorted (address, checksum) pairs.

sources.notes: Assessed at crc-sdk 0.11.2: the statement, the code references and the records below describe that version. The port to 1.0 is pending. Draft. NOAA lists 126 stations with this product; ten are in Texas. A station without the product is answered with HTTP 200 and an empty body of the usual shape, which crc-sdk refuses. NOAA sends no ETag and no Last-Modified for these responses. The exceedance levels carry the datum label in capitals (MHHW) and the annual series in lower case (mhhw); crc-sdk passes both on as published. NOAA sometimes answers the same address with the values rounded to one decimal instead of two or three (seen 2026-11-12); crc-sdk delivers whichever answer it received.
sources.purpose: NOAA's published exceedance levels and annual extremes at tide stations, as published.

statement.text: Accepts a station only as a string of exactly seven digits 0-9; anything else raises ValueError before any request.

Makes three GET requests to `https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/dpapi/prod/webapi/product.json` with `name=extremewaterlevels`, the station and `units=metric`: one with nothing more (station), one with `details=exceedancelevels&levelType=high` (levels), one with `extremeType=annuals&levelType=high` (annuals). Low-water and monthly products are never requested.

statement.note: The check compares with a second download of the same address, so it also differs when NOAA answers the same address differently (step one-answer); it cannot tell the two apart.
statement.text: Saves each response unchanged as `source.json` and records its SHA-256 in a manifest beside it.
Asks each address once and takes that answer as the station's published values. Nothing asks a second time or compares two answers; the recorded SHA-256 is that of the one answer received.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: NOAA's responses are a few kilobytes and complete. No constructed test was written for it.
statement.text: Refuses a response longer than 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) or shorter than its announced Content-Length.

statement.note: On NOAA's data two of these rules fire: an empty station list (a station without the product) and a levels response without the station id (NOAA sent an error message in its place). Each of the other rules is confirmed on constructed responses only, in the tests.
statement.text: Refuses a station (ValueError, nothing cached) unless: the station response lists exactly one station with that id, a longitude in -180..180, a latitude in -90..90 and a non-empty epoch; the levels and annuals responses carry that id, `units` equal to `meters` and a non-empty datum; the two datum labels are equal when letter case is ignored; the annuals response has a non-empty notice, a trend that is null or a number, and for every extreme an integer year and a finite value; the levels response has a non-empty `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels` in which every probability is in (0, 1] and not repeated, every return period is at least 1, every level is finite, and a confidence bound that is present lies on its side of the level. There is no rule about the length or completeness of the annual series.

`source_levels()` gives one row per entry of `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels`, in NOAA's order, with eleven columns: the station id, then name, longitude, latitude and datum epoch from the station response repeated on every row, the datum label from the levels response, and NOAA's `probability`, `returnPeriod`, `level`, `lower90CI` and `upper90CI`. A missing confidence bound becomes null. The return period is NOAA's rounded label, not 1/probability. `GEV_LO` and the monthly groups are not delivered.

`annual_extremes()` gives one row per entry of `extremes` in the annuals response, in NOAA's order, with six columns: the station id, `year`, `value`, the datum label from the annuals response, the datum epoch from the station response and NOAA's notice repeated on every row. No year is added, dropped or filled.
Delivers numbers as 64-bit floats (the year as a 32-bit integer) with NOAA's values: nothing is rounded, no unit is converted (metres are requested and required) and no datum is transformed.

`source_info()` gives the whole station entry as NOAA sent it, the datum label and units of the levels response, and the trend, its units, its start and end dates and the notice of the annuals response. The trend (mm/yr) appears here only, not in the tables.

Writes for each response a manifest with the address, station id, resource name, SHA-256, retrieval time, ETag, Last-Modified, an attribution, a documentation address and a terms address. The tables themselves carry no metadata.
With `cache(dir, sha256={resource: digest})` a response whose SHA-256 is not the given one is refused with RuntimeError; the names accepted are station, levels and annuals.

statement.note: Read in the code and in crc-sdk's own test (tests/test_noaa_water_levels.py), not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to fail or change between two requests.
statement.text: Keeps the three responses of one fetch together as one snapshot; `refresh` fetches all three again, moves a pointer to the new snapshot and deletes the old one, and a fetch that fails leaves the previous snapshot in place.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to change a response between two runs. Left to monitoring.
statement.text: In `reuse` mode (the default) a complete cached snapshot is served without asking NOAA whether the responses have changed. NOAA sends neither ETag nor Last-Modified for them.

sources.adds: From NOAA's hourly station reports crc-sdk makes, per station position and year, the highest daily maximum or the lowest daily minimum temperature of the year, using its own rules for which reports, days and years count. By default a day counts only when all 24 hours hold an accepted report and a year only when every day counts; a year that falls short keeps its row with no value, its coverage and the reason. No curve is fitted unless the user asks for one. The hourly reports themselves are not in the output.
sources.compared: Every station-year of forty Texas stations, 2000 to 2024, is recomputed in Python from NOAA's files with the stated rules and compared with crc-sdk's annual samples, field by field, for both indicators, at the default completeness and at a relaxed one (90 per cent of days); a sample is recomputed again from NOAA's second file format. The stations crc-sdk selects in the box are compared with NOAA's station list, the metadata with the statement, and the checksums crc-sdk records with the reference's own downloads.
sources.notes: Assessed on the sample of crc-sdk 0.11.2, so that the two versions can be compared: the first forty USW stations of NOAA's station list in the Texas box, 2000 to 2024. These are small airports whose records begin around 2005 (592 of 1,000 station-years had a file at the 0.11.2 run). What crc-sdk 1.0 returns by default is checked: annual samples, not a fitted curve. Two default rules are stricter than in 0.11: a day needs all 24 hours (0.11: 18) and a year needs every day (0.11: 90 per cent), so few station-years of these airports carry a value by default; the assessment therefore also checks Coverage.minimum_fraction(0.9), which matches 0.11's year rule but not its day rule. Days are UTC days: in Texas a UTC day runs from the local evening to the next. The values are extremes of sampled hourly temperature, not of an instrument's daily maximum and minimum.
sources.purpose: Annual extremes of hourly station temperature per station and year, as a local check on gridded curves.

statement.text: Selects stations from NOAA's station list `hourly/doc/ghcnh-station-list.csv` (GHCN_ID, NAME, LONGITUDE, LATITUDE): by identifier, where an identifier not in the list stops the read, or by area, keeping the stations whose listed position lies in the box, edges included, in the list's order. A listed position with a coordinate missing or outside WGS84 is dropped, so that station is never selected by area; a blank name is replaced by the identifier.

Requests one Parquet file per station and year, `hourly/access/by-year/<year>/parquet/GHCNh_<station>_<year>.parquet`, downloads the whole file (60-second timeout, no second try) and keeps it in its cache under its SHA-256. A file NOAA does not have (HTTP 404) is recorded as absent; any other HTTP or network error stops the read.
Reads seven columns: STATION, DATE, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, temperature, temperature_Quality_Code and temperature_Source_Code. A file without them stops the read. ELEVATION is not read.

Stops the read of the whole selection, with no rows, when a file holds a report of another station or of another year, a DATE it cannot read, a coordinate missing or outside WGS84, a temperature that is not a finite number, or two reports with the same time at the same position. A report with no temperature is kept with no value.

statement.note: Unchanged from 0.11. In NOAA's files the source lists may not be put to the test (at 0.11.2 no report had code 1 or 5 from an unlisted source); the offline tests exercise them on constructed files.
statement.text: Uses a temperature when its quality code (spaces stripped) is blank, or is 1 from one of fourteen listed source codes, or is 5 from one of eight listed source codes. Any other code keeps the report with no value.
Uses a temperature only if it lies between -93.2 and 61.8 degrees Celsius inclusive; outside, the report is kept with no value.
Takes the temperature in degrees Celsius as published; nothing is converted. The output variable is `noaa:ghcnh:<indicator>`, declared as a temperature in degC.

Groups the accepted reports of each position by the calendar day of DATE as published, which is UTC; no time zone is applied. For each day it counts the distinct clock hours that hold an accepted report.

Counts a day as complete only when all 24 clock hours hold an accepted report; several reports in one hour count once. The daily maximum (or minimum) is taken over every accepted report of a complete day; an incomplete day has no value. This rule is fixed: `Coverage` does not change it.

Counts a year as complete by the `Coverage` given to `GHCNh`: by default `Coverage.complete()`, every day of the year complete (365 of 365, 366 of 366); with `Coverage.minimum_fraction(f)`, complete days divided by the days of the year at least f. A year with no complete day is never complete.

For a complete year, takes the highest daily maximum (`annual_maximum_daily_maximum_temperature`) or the lowest daily minimum (`annual_minimum_daily_minimum_temperature`) over the complete days. An incomplete year keeps its row with no value, failure `incomplete_year`, and its coverage: complete days, days of the year and the fraction required.

Gives each distinct reported position its own support: `<station>@` and the first 20 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the position as a little-endian WKB point, with its H3 cell at resolution 9. A station that moves within a year gets one row per position, each reduced over its own reports only; no move is refused and positions are not merged. Elevation is not carried.

Returns `Samples`: one row per position and year, with the year as time, the value, its coverage and failure, the station and support identifiers, the H3 cell and the point; declared as annual values with an upper tail for the maximum and a lower tail for the minimum. A station-year with no file, or with a file holding no report, has no row: it is an `UnavailableStationYear` diagnostic, counted as requested and incomplete. The report counts requested, produced, no-data, usable and incomplete years. No curve is fitted: that needs an explicit `fit(SampleFit(...))`.

Records with the output every resource read: the station list and every station-year file requested, absent ones included, each with its address, SHA-256, retrieval time, the licence text `NOAA open-use terms; originator terms may apply` and the attribution `NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information and NOAA CO-OPS; original source records retained.`, and a release identifier with a SHA-256 over them all. No GHCNh version is recorded.

sources.adds: From crc-sdk 1.0 nothing is added to the depths: each pixel of JRC's maps comes back with the depths the publisher gives at its return periods, placed at probabilities 1 - 1/T, with an identifier built from the pixel's position, the H3 cell of its centre and its outline. A pixel with fewer than two depths, or with a depth lower than one at a shorter return period, is left out and counted. Up to 0.11 crc-sdk fitted a Gumbel curve per pixel; that assessment is kept as the previous version.
sources.compared: JRC's files are read whole by an independent reader. In five areas (Texas, Houston, Austin, Fremont, the Rhine) the reader decides for every pixel whether it should be delivered and with which depths, and that is compared with crc-sdk's rows pixel by pixel. The pixels requested, the files read, the identifiers, the cells, the release, the licence and the recorded provenance are checked separately, as is a box outside a product's coverage.
sources.notes: Assessed at crc-sdk 1.0.0 on the default path, where nothing is fitted. The explicit fit, `fit(QuantileFit(...))`, is not assessed yet. The review maps and the comparisons with FEMA zones, USGS gauges and Harvey marks were made from crc-sdk 0.11 output and are shown with the previous version. On 2026-11-24 the publisher's server did not answer, so crc-sdk read the copy of the publisher's files held from 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-23; its own downloads were not exercised.

sources.purpose: River flood depth at the publisher's return periods, per pixel of the publisher's maps, as the knots of a quantile curve. Nothing is fitted unless the user asks.

statement.text: Reads the publisher's README.txt, for GloFAS the tile index `tile_extents.geojson`, and one depth file per return period written in the code (GloFAS 10, 20, 50, 75, 100, 200, 500 years; EFAS also 30 and 40) for every GloFAS tile whose extent meets the box, or for EFAS the one continental file.

statement.note: Not exercised on 2026-11-24: the publisher's server did not answer, so crc-sdk read the copy of the publisher's files held. The values it decoded from those files are compared in the values checks.
statement.text: Reads each depth file by range requests for the window of the box only, pinned to the file's ETag so that a file changed during the read is refused.
Reads the release from the README (the text after 'Dataset version') and refuses to run when it is not the one written in the code (GloFAS 2.1.2, EFAS 3.1.1). The file addresses hold no version.
Takes every pixel of the publisher's grid that the box touches.
Treats the file's nodata value and non-finite values as no depth.
Returns a row for a pixel that has two or more depths, none lower than a depth at a shorter return period. Every other pixel is left out.
Counts the pixels left out and reports the number once for the read, in a warning that names both reasons together. Pixels that are simply dry are in the same number.
Places a depth published for the return period T at the probability 1 - 1/T. A return period with no depth at the pixel gives no knot.
Returns the publisher's depths unchanged, in metres.
Names the pixel `jrc:<product>:<tile>:<row>:<column>` by its row and column in the publisher's file (`continental` for EFAS), so that the same pixel has the same name whatever box asked for it.
Gives each row the H3 cell of resolution 9 that holds the centre of the pixel, and the pixel's outline as its geometry.
Fits nothing: every row holds a quantile curve made of the published knots, and no fit and no failure.
Labels every row with the variable `jrc:<product>:flood_depth` and with no scenario and no period.

Records the Open Database License (`ODbL-1.0`) for every file, with the attribution 'Copernicus Emergency Management Service; European Commission Joint Research Centre'. The licence is written in the code and is not read from the publisher.
Records for every file its address, a SHA-256, the licence, the attribution and the retrieval time. For a depth file the checksum is of the window crc-sdk cut from it, not of the publisher's file.
For a box that lies outside a product's coverage, returns no rows and raises no error.

sources.adds: From NASA's daily files crc-sdk makes one row per grid cell of a box and year: the largest one-day or five-day rainfall, or the hottest or the coldest day, after converting units. It reads the newest file version NASA lists for each year, keeps a cell's value only when every day (every five-day window) of the year is present, and gives a cell without a value a row with the reason. Nothing is fitted. What it acquired is kept in its own cache when one is given.
sources.compared: For one model and member in the Texas box, two years and the four indicators, the reference reader lists NASA's bucket itself, downloads the whole file crc-sdk read, and recomputes every grid cell's annual value, coverage, edges and H3 cell, compared value by value with crc-sdk's rows. Which file version each side read, the file's own identity attributes, the labels and provenance, a year without a file, a model with a 365-day calendar, and the file versions NASA serves are checked separately.
sources.notes: Assessed on one model and member (ACCESS-CM2, r1i1p1f1), the Texas box, 2014 of the historical run and 2050 of ssp585: the sample of the run on crc-sdk 0.11.2 (2,332 grid cells, 2,158 on land), whose records are kept under records/0.11.2/. crc-sdk 1.0 reads NASA's version 2.0 files for this sample where 0.11 read version 1.0 by default, so the values differ between the two runs by what NASA changed between the versions (the exploration tables show by how much). crc-sdk 1.0 takes no file version, no grid label and, by default, requires every day of the year; `Coverage.minimum_fraction` and `observations()` were not assessed. Scenario, model and member are free text in 1.0 and are not read by the detector. Each result is one model and one member, not an ensemble. Ocean cells carry no value. The licence written in the files (`cmip6_license`) differs by file while NASA states the archive is CC0.
sources.purpose: Annual extremes from bias-adjusted, downscaled daily model output at 0.25 degree, one model and member at a time.

statement.note: NASA's files are stored in chunks of one day by the whole globe, so a box of any size reads every chunk of the file (about 240 requests for a 247 MB file).
statement.text: Lists NASA's bucket (S3 ListObjectsV2, page by page) under `<model>/<scenario>/<member>/<variable>/`, then reads one NetCDF file per year by HTTP range requests of 1 MiB with `If-Match` on the ETag, checking size and validator before and after. NASA's whole file is neither downloaded nor checksummed; crc-sdk caches and checksums the window it cuts from it.
For each year, reads the file with the highest version in NASA's listing, the version being taken from the file name (no suffix is 1.0, `_v<version>` otherwise).
Takes no file version: an older revision NASA still serves cannot be requested.

statement.note: That no comparison is made is shown in the offline tests, on a file that names another member.
statement.text: Takes the model, scenario and member from the request and the listing address, and labels the result with them; the file's own identity attributes are not compared with the request.

statement.note: Asked for one model with a 365-day calendar (BCC-CSM2-MR, its header only); models with a 360-day calendar were not asked for.
statement.text: Reads the calendar from the header of the earliest year's file and refuses the series unless it is Gregorian (`standard`, `gregorian` or `proleptic_gregorian`); each year's file must declare the same calendar.

statement.note: The files read have 365 days and no gap. A day absent from the time axis and a leap year were exercised only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Decodes `days since <date>` to whole days (the stamp is floored), requires them to be unique and increasing, and keeps a day of the year only when exactly one time step falls in it.

Copies a global `license` (or `licence`) attribute, when the file has one, onto the file's resource as its licence. NASA's files carry the model licence as `cmip6_license`, which is not read; NASA's statement that the archive is CC0 is not recorded.
Requires precipitation to declare exactly `kg m-2 s-1` and multiplies it by 86,400 to give millimetres per day.
Requires temperature to declare exactly `K` (bytes are decoded to text first) and subtracts 273.15 to give degrees Celsius.

statement.note: A box across the 180 degree meridian was not run.
statement.text: Selects every grid cell whose rectangle (edges halfway between neighbouring centres) intersects or touches the box; longitudes are brought to -180..180. Rows follow the file's latitude order and, within a row, its column order.
Treats values equal to the file's `_FillValue` or `missing_value`, and non-finite values, as missing (after `scale_factor` and `add_offset`, when present).

statement.note: In NASA's files a cell has every day or none (ocean), so a partly complete cell was exercised only in the offline tests.
statement.text: By default (`Coverage.complete()`) gives a cell a value only when every day of the year is present; for rx5day, every five-day window that lies within the year (365 days give 361 windows).

`rx1day` is the largest daily value of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum of five consecutive days within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years. A negative precipitation value makes the whole read fail.
`txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.

Returns one row per selected grid cell and year, with or without a value: the cell's rectangle as geometry, its H3 cell (resolution 9) at the centre, `support_id` `nex:0p25:<row>:<column>` (its place in NASA's file), the time as the year, the value, the coverage (valid and expected days or windows, the minimum fraction) and, for a cell without a value, the failure `incomplete_year`. No distribution is fitted.

statement.note: Asked for one year after the end of the historical run (2015); a year before the first file was not asked for.
statement.text: A year NASA has no file for is not refused: crc-sdk reads the nearest year's file to place the cells and returns every cell without a value (failure `incomplete_year`, 0 days present).

Labels every row with the variable `nex:<indicator>`, the scenario and a period; the metadata names the unit (degC or mm), the calendar, the model, the member and the release `<model>/<scenario>/<member>/<variable>`.

statement.note: The release checksum and the checksum of each window are crc-sdk's own encodings and were not recomputed.
statement.text: Records the unit conversion and the annual reduction (with its coverage rule) as provenance, and as resources: the listing page, the release (a checksum of every year's file name and ETag), the header read and the window cut from each file, each with its address and retrieval time and the attribution 'NASA Earth Exchange NEX-GDDP-CMIP6' on the release and the window.
